artworks.title: Sleeping Hermaphroditus
artworks.artist: Unknown (Roman copy); mattress by Gian Lorenzo Bernini
artworks.description: The Borghese Hermaphrodite in the Louvre — Hellenistic languor with Bernini's buttoned mattress — Salmacis' embrace made marble.

artworks.title: Sleeping Hermaphroditus (Palazzo Massimo)
artworks.artist: Roman copy after a Hellenistic original
artworks.year: 2nd century AD (copy); Greek original 2nd century BC
artworks.description: A second Roman Imperial marble of the Sleeping Hermaphroditus type, displayed in the Palazzo Massimo alle Terme in Rome. Like the more famous Borghese–Louvre example, it shows the figure reclining face-down, the dual sex revealed only as the viewer circles — Hellenistic erotic surprise preserved in another Imperial copy.

artworks.title: Hermaphroditus and the Nymph Salmacis
artworks.description: An oil by the Prague Mannerist Bartholomeus Spranger in the Kunsthistorisches Museum, Vienna. Salmacis coils around the resisting youth at the fountain that will fuse them — Ovid's Carian episode painted as courtly erotic entanglement, Hermaphroditus still distinct in the moment before the waters change his form.

artworks.title: The Nymph Salmacis and Hermaphroditus
artworks.description: A Neoclassical oil by François-Joseph Navez in the Museum of Fine Arts, Ghent. Salmacis embraces Hermaphroditus at the spring's edge — cool marble flesh and still water staging Ovid's metamorphosis as a quiet, almost sculptural encounter rather than a violent fusion.

popCulture.title: Sleeping Hermaphroditus
popCulture.description: The Borghese Hermaphrodite — Hellenistic languor on Bernini's mattress — remains the figure's defining afterlife in marble.

popCulture.title: Hermaphroditus
popCulture.description: Child of Hermes and Aphrodite — Salmacis' fountain still supplies the vocabulary for dual-sexed form.

popCulture.title: Metamorphoses
popCulture.creator: Ovid
popCulture.description: Book IV's Carian episode — the nymph who will not let go — is still the canonical telling of Hermaphroditus' change.
